p.i: Flumen ab illustri deferitur jugere Fletus
Ervetus hunc rapido gratior amne vorat.
Qui dum progreditur labente valentior unda
Hunc subito Rheni lava furore bibit.

main_text.p: Imperii Neapolitani, Coniugis Sue- cie, & Rayneli, ... de Floridis, ... coquo utriusque Regis ... Iure in Ponte i Sicilia.
main_text.head: Quo sequitur ... Gruiis ... Aduersaria.
main_text.p: In quo anno Nuptie ... et aliquid Caluni, nuc orta- rum, Ruina a Ioachy ... ut pro Iure Consilijs in finitope Patre, Cuius ... Nepotum ... Ius Relique.
main_text.head: SOMNIVM.
main_text.p: Ex tribus ... Aduersis ... Nouis ... Verbis quibus ... pellendis ... Gentes ... Regno ... ut ... Ut ... ex ... ad ... sunt ... quam ... Deus ... meritis ... iudicium.
Mauult hunc ... ergo ... Ad ... Caesarum ... quam ... ... ... ... ... ...

page.notes: The first word of the page header is printed as "PARS SECUNDA." with the numeral 371 at the right. Some verse lines are doubtful in places (for example "Eiphalie", "Lechminum", "Caftera", "adcomitum", "Maenia"), as they are blurred and show-through from the reverse side overlaps the text. The lower woodcut ornament carries no text. Much of this part is badly faded and damaged; the Latin of the body text after the heading is largely illegible and the transcription of the lower paragraphs is approximate. The large initial I is woodcut and joined to SOMNIVM. Upper lines are partly obscured by the ornament.
